title: Shapley value and integral differ
statement: On subsets of a one-element set, let $f(S)=1$ when the element belongs to $S$ and $f(S)=0$ otherwise. Its Shapley value, defined as the expected marginal over a subset chosen uniformly among all subsets, is not equal to four times the integral from $0$ to $1$ of $p(1-p)$ times the Bernoulli subset expectation of the squared marginal $(f(S\cup\{0\})-f(S\setminus\{0\}))^2$, where a subset $S$ has weight $p^{|S|}(1-p)^{1-|S|}$.
hypotheses_covered: The ground set is the one-element set
The function is the indicator that the element belongs to the subset
